specialRules.ruleFull: A Dwarf is taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 is knocked down, 3-5 stunned, 6 out of action.
A Dwarf ignores the special rules for maces, clubs and the like.
The warband may never include an Elven Hired Sword or Dramatis Persona of any kind.
If the warband routs voluntarily, it receives half the exploration dice, rounding up.
Unless a rule says otherwise, every member of the warband is immune to all psychology, frenzy and stupidity included, and never tests for fighting alone.
A Slayer may never use armour of any kind, and may use no magic except magic weapons.

A Slayer may use only thrown missile weapons and pistols of any kind. Only the Gunners and the Master Gunner may learn Shooting skills, and only they may use thrown weapons and gunpowder weapons; they may use no other missile weapon.
The warband captures Swabbies, under the Sartosa campaign rules. A willing captive joins the Landlubbers; an unwilling one becomes a Thaggi.
Any warrior within 6" of the Slayer Captain may use his Leadership instead of his own.

Every Pistol in the warband, of any kind, has its range increased by 3", and every Blunderbuss, of any kind, by 6". The increase holds only while the Master Gunner is in the warband, and only in a battle he was deployed in.

Gunners do not have the Death Wish skill and suffer psychology as normal. When a Gunner gains That Lad's Got Talent, he must learn Death Wish instead of rolling on the Hero advance table, even if Special is not one of his two skill lists.

Landlubbers do not have the Death Wish skill and suffer psychology as normal. When a Landlubber gains That Lad's Got Talent, he must learn Death Wish instead of rolling on the Hero advance table, even if Special is not one of his two skill lists.
Thaggi are not hired: they are given to the warband, under the Sartosa campaign rules.
Thaggi need not be armed alike: each may carry different equipment, but only from the Thaggi Equipment list. A Thaggi may never use magic or cast a spell.
If the warband routs, any Thaggi who has already left the table in an earlier turn escapes for good: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specialRules.rulename: 'Don't mind them mates, they ain't true dwarves!'
specialRules.ruleFull: Thaggi who are running away or have been taken out of action do not count towards the warband's rout test.

specialSkillsList.name: Deathwish
specialSkillsList.description: The Hero is immune to all psychology and never tests for fighting alone.

specialSkillsList.name: Gloryseeker
specialSkillsList.description: While the Pirate is in close combat with a model that causes fear, he has +1 Attack each round of combat. He gains one extra Attack only, however many fear-causing enemies he faces.

specialSkillsList.name: Leviathan Slayer
specialSkillsList.description: In hand-to-hand combat the Slayer always wounds on a 5+, after bonuses and penalties. If he would need 4+ or less to wound, he causes a critical hit on a natural 5+ instead.

rules.name: Reload
rules.text: A Dwarven Pistol may be fired and reloaded in the same turn. A hero with the Pistolier skill and a brace of Dwarven Pistols may fire twice each turn, no more.
As the Mordheim rulebook has it.
As the Mordheim rulebook has it.

rules.name: Well Built
rules.text: Whenever a Dwarven Pistol misfires, roll a D6: on a 4+ the misfire is ignored. Refined Powder has no effect on a Dwarven Pistol.

rules.name: Shot
rules.text: When the model fires, draw a straight line 16" long and 1" wide in any direction from him: every model in its path is hit automatically at Strength 3.

rules.name: Fire Twice
rules.text: Either barrel takes a long time to load, so it may be fired only twice in a battle. The user may instead fire both shots at once, dealing 2 Strength 3 hits instead of 1.

rules.name: Misfire
rules.text: The blunderbuss needs no roll to hit, but roll a D6 anyway: on a 1 it misfires, and you roll once on the black powder misfire table.

flags.what: The skill table is text (X ticks), read from the -layout text. The Pirate column, which this PDF does not print a skill list for, is ticked for all three Heroes and is left out: see the decisions.
Sea Trollslayers are listed with the Heroes' starting experience (0) but have no row in the skill table and no limit on their number, so they are read as henchmen.
A Slayer warband needs at least 3 models: our templates hold no minimum, so it is not imported. No henchmen group sizes and no maximum profile are printed: the crew takes our Dwarf race.
Thaggi are described as dwarfs that humans also fill out: they take our Dwarf race, as their profile (M3 T4) is a dwarf's.
Thaggi have no hire price (they are given to the warband, not hired): their cost is 0 gc.

Up Close is printed as "Only Gunners and the Master gunners may only learn Shooting Skills, and may any thrown weapons and gunpowder weapons (no other types.)": read as the Gunners and the Master Gunner alone learning Shooting skills and using thrown and gunpowder weapons.
The Dwarf Axe's line is 15 gc, Rare 9; ours is 15 gc, Rare 8, which is unchanged, so the warband buys from a price row of its own at Rare 9.

The Dwarven Pistol (30 gc, 60 for a brace) and the Double-barreled Blunderbuss (60 gc) are stubs: the PDF prints no rules and we hold neither. The Gunner list sells the Dueling Pistol beside the Dwarven Pistol, so they are not the same weapon.

The Pirate and Gunner lists print "Armour . . . None". The Thaggi list's Missile Weapons and Armour (Buckler 5 gc, Toughened Leathers 5 gc) are printed at the top of the right column, continuing the left column; read that way, which matches the warband rule that Slayers wear no armour.
"Harpoon (Javelin)" at 5 gc is our Javelins, and "Throwing Axe" at 15 gc our Throwing Axes, each shown under the list's name.
Hard to Kill, Hard Head, Grudgebearers and Deathwish are printed as the warband's rules, and are kept as warband rules rather than copied onto each fighter.
Throwing Axes are a stub of the Dwarf Slayer Cult's (2a), declared here too so the Slayer Pirates buy them at 15 gc; neither PDF prints rules for them.
The PDF spells the skill "Death Wish"; it is the Dwarf Slayer Cult's Deathwish, one skill with the same words in both groups, and who may take it sits in each group's note.

The Pirate column is the Pirate Skills list of the Sartosa campaign rules (Sartosa Skills, Hired Swords and Dramatis Personae, p1-2), not this PDF: it is the shared Sartosa Pirate Skills group, declared in sartosan-pirates.json and named by each hero who ticks it.

The Dwarven Pistol's rules are in the Sartosa campaign rules' Equipment PDF (p3): 6", Strength 4, Reload, Save Modifier, Hand-to-hand and Well Built. Its trading-list price there is 40 gc, Rare 10 (80 for a brace), which the item takes; the warband's own line stays 30 gc, 60 for a brace, as a starting price.

The Double-barreled Blunderbuss's rules are in the Sartosa campaign rules' Equipment PDF (p1): Strength 3, Shot, Fire Twice and Misfire. Its trading-list price (p10) is 60 gc, Rare 11, the same as the line's.
Throwing Axes are 15 gc, Rare 5 in the Sartosa campaign rules' Equipment PDF's trading list (p10), so the warband's row is Rare 5.

the Sartosa campaign rules' Equipment PDF's trading list (p10) prints the Dwarven Axe at 15 gc, Rare 8, Dwarves only, as ours is; this warband's own list prints Rare 9, which its price row keeps. The warband PDF's number stands.

The Sartosa campaign rules' Equipment PDF (p10) prints one trading list for the whole setting. William, 11 Nov 2026 (decision 20): it goes in as price rows for the Sartosa warband types, and our own prices and rarities never change. Each item below is one the setting's shop prices differently from ours; every one of the eleven Sartosa types carries the same rows, declared in its own file, and a warband's own list price still wins for that warband.
